analysis:
The PR changes one documentation line in docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (line 689). The gpt-oss-20b checkpoint-size row now reads bf16 K/V on all 24 layers, with 3.15 MB fixed state, 25.17 MB full rows per 1,024 tokens (24,576 B/token) and a 154.1 MB file at 6,144 tokens. It was previously float32 on 23 of 24 layers, at roughly double those sizes. The edit is a documentation-only sizing correction. It changes no code, no environment gating, no TTL (30 minutes), no HMAC lookup-tag derivation, no DBK3 AAD, no cacheSalt scoping and no disk-budget policy.

Checked against T-041, the only retrieved definition. The change does not widen the at-rest surface or the cross-tenant TTFT oracle (SEC-035), and it does not alter the mitigations. The smaller checkpoint size would, if the underlying code change exists, slightly reduce disk and write wear and the transient staging reservation. The docs assert that the checkpoint dtype is now bf16, but the code change that makes this true is not in the supplied evidence. Any related dtype or checkpoint-layout change in provider-swift (storage identity, compatibility fingerprint) was not supplied and should be reviewed in its own batch. The doc line 689 is consistent with the surrounding text, which says the paged probe observes native per-layer types and that the storage identity includes every layer's dtype. A nonempty DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV_DTYPE override of float16 or float32 would not match a bf16 layer, but that is a documentation or code consistency question and not a security regression. No findings.
